title: Unify clover workflow environment setup at workflows
description:
We currently set up PostgreSQL, Ruby, Clover, and databases separately
in each workflow using the same steps. To simplify and standardize this,
we’re extracting these steps into a shared action.

Notably, we install PostgreSQL directly on the system instead of using a
Docker container for three main reasons:

  1. Reusable workflows don’t support GitHub Action's `services`
     feature.
  2. macOS runners are free for open source projects and help us catch
     platform-specific issues. However, they don’t come with Docker due
     to licensing restrictions, making container-based setups more
     difficult.
  3. Our controlplane tests have been taking longer. To support running
     tests in parallel, we need more flexible database configurations
     than what the default Docker setup allows.

This change should reduce duplication, simplify maintenance, and improve
testing flexibility across platforms.
ellipsis_summary:
Unifies environment setup for workflows by introducing a shared `setup-clover` action, replacing redundant setup steps, and removing Docker-based PostgreSQL configurations.
> 
>   - **Environment Setup**:
>     - Introduces `setup-clover` action in `.github/actions/setup-clover/action.yml` to unify PostgreSQL, Ruby, and Clover database setup.
>     - Installs PostgreSQL directly on the system instead of using Docker due to GitHub Actions limitations and macOS runner constraints.
>   - **Workflow Changes**:
>     - Replaces individual setup steps with `setup-clover` action in `ci.yml`, `cli-ci.yml`, `e2e.yml`, and `respirate-ci.yml`.
>     - Removes Docker-based PostgreSQL setup and related environment variables from these workflows.
>   - **Benefits**:
>     - Reduces duplication and simplifies maintenance.
>     - Enhances testing flexibility across platforms by allowing more flexible database configurations.
> 
>

(e.g. fw add-rule -s/-e), and for regular arguments that should

* invalid/duplicate/missing fields used when multiple fields
  separated by a comma is allowed

title: Give free premium runner upgrade for new installations for 7 days
description:
-(REMOVED) ~**Fix free premium runner upgrade logic**~
  ~If a free premium upgrade is enabled for an installation, we bill based
  on the original VM size, not the upgraded one.~
  
  ~Previously, runners were upgraded during provisioning when the free
  upgrade was active. However, if the upgrade expired before the runner
  was destroyed, we ended up charging based on the upgraded VM size, since
  the upgrade was no longer active at billing time.~
  
  ~To fix this, we now determine the billed_vm_size at provisioning time
  and store it. This ensures consistent billing, regardless of the upgrade
  status at the time of destruction.~
  
  ~I didn’t remove the old billing logic yet, because runners already
  provisioned before this change won’t have a billed_vm_size set. If the
  column is empty, we still fall back to the old logic. I’ll remove the
  fallback after confirming all active runners have the new column
  populated.~
  

- **Give free premium runner upgrade for new installations for 7 days**
  If a GitHub installation was created within the past 7 days,
  automatically grant a free premium runner upgrade to allow users to try
  out enhanced performance.
  

- **Show badge on UI for free premium upgrades**
  
| No runner | Settings |
|--------|-------|
| ![empty-runner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd65dfe8-ae78-40f9-aaf5-4e894d54539b) | ![settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/196620c8-e83a-456f-8b82-10106fbc892f) |

- (NEW) **Fix free premium runner upgrade logic**

If a free premium upgrade is enabled for an installation, we bill based
on the original VM size, not the upgraded one.

Previously, runners were upgraded during provisioning when the free
upgrade was active. However, if the upgrade expired before the runner
was destroyed, we ended up charging based on the upgraded VM size, since
the upgrade was no longer active at billing time.

To fix this, we check the free upgrade expiration time against the runner creation time, not the current time.
ellipsis_summary:
----

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Introduces a 7-day free premium runner upgrade for new installations and updates billing logic to ensure correct charges, with UI changes to display eligibility badges.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:
>     - New installations receive a free premium runner upgrade for 7 days (`github_installation.rb`).
>     - Billing logic updated to charge based on original VM size, not upgraded size, if free upgrade is active (`github_runner.rb`).
>   - **UI**:
>     - Displays badge for free premium upgrade eligibility in `runner.erb` and `setting.erb`.
>   - **Tests**:
>     - Updated tests in `github_runner_spec.rb` and `github_spec.rb` to cover new billing logic and UI changes.
> 
>

title: Add support for authentication using OIDC
description:
This supports dynamic client registration with an OIDC provider. After the OIDC provider has been added, users who would like to login with it can go to a provider specific login page (`/auth/$provider_ubid`).  They can then click the button on the page to start the OIDC login flow. This is a suboptimial login flow. We should switch to multiphase login, where a user enters their email, and after they enter the email, they are shown authentication options for the account.  The OIDC-provider specific page will still be needed for account creation with that approach, but not for general login.

This uses omniauth like the current social logins.  It requires the omniauth_openid_connect gem, which has a bunch of dependencies we would prefer to avoid, such as activesupport. Long term, we'd like to cut down on the dependencies, but I'm not sure how feasible that is. **Support for this has now been implemented in this PR.**

Omniauth is designed around a fixed list of providers, not a dynamic list, so currently, after adding a provider, you must restart the app to be able to login with it. This is a high priority to fix, but it may take a while as Omniauth is not designed for it. **Support for this has now been implemented in this PR.**

Currently, if a user already has an account, they cannot login using an OIDC provider. In order to allow that, we'd need to support registration with the OIDC after login, similar to the social logins.  **Support for this has now been implemented in this PR.**

OIDC providers may not necessarily provide account names, only emails, so this changes the omniauth account creation to generate an account name from an email. I'm not sure if a user can currently change the name of their account, but we should probably add support for that.
ellipsis_summary:
Adds OIDC authentication support with dynamic client registration, allowing users to login via OIDC providers and manage connections in their account settings.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:
>     - Adds OIDC authentication support using `omniauth_openid_connect` gem.
>     - Users can login via OIDC providers through `/auth/$provider_ubid`.
>     - Requires app restart after adding a provider due to Omniauth limitations.
>     - Generates account names from emails if not provided by OIDC.
>   - **Models**:
>     - Adds `OidcProvider` model in `oidc_provider.rb` for managing OIDC providers.
>     - Supports dynamic client registration and manual creation of OIDC providers.
>   - **Routes**:
>     - Updates `routes/account.rb` to handle OIDC login and disconnection.
>     - Adds OIDC login page rendering in `clover.rb`.
>   - **Views**:
>     - Updates `login_method.erb` to include OIDC provider connection options.
>     - Adds `oidc_login.erb` for OIDC login page.
>   - **Tests**:
>     - Adds tests in `oidc_provider_spec.rb` for OIDC provider registration and error handling.
>     - Adds tests in `auth_spec.rb` for OIDC login and account connection/disconnection.
> 
>

title: Use FOR NO KEY UPDATE instead of FOR UPDATE
description: FOR UPDATE takes stronger locks, and is only needed if you plan on deleting the row or modifying one of key columns.  If you use FOR UPDATE, you block other transactions insert rows that reference a row using a FOR UPDATE lock.  From looking at these cases, I don't think that is the case, so using FOR NO KEY UPDATE should allow the assurances we need without unnecessarily blocking other concurrent transactions.
ellipsis_summary:
Change `FOR UPDATE` to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in several models to reduce lock strength and improve concurrency.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:
>     - Change `FOR UPDATE` to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in `setup_blob_storage` in `github_repository.rb`, `TAKE_LEASE_PS` in `strand.rb`, `pick_vm` in `vm_pool.rb`, and `setup_prepared_statements` in `dispatcher.rb`.
>     - This change reduces lock strength, allowing more concurrent transactions without blocking inserts that reference locked rows.
>   - **Tests**:
>     - Update test in `vm_pool_spec.rb` to expect `for_no_key_update` instead of `for_update`.
> 
>

title: Give explicit description to runner script service
description:
Previously, if no description was provided, the service used the full
command as the description. Since the command includes the JIT token,
and GitHub recently increased the token length. This resulted in overly
long descriptions.

More importantly, including the token in the description is not ideal
from a security and clarity standpoint. To address this, we now assign a
default, explicit description instead.
ellipsis_summary:

>

>     - Prevents JIT token from being included in service description for security and clarity.
>   - **Tests**:

title: Pass JIT config via file to runner script
description:
Previously, we passed the JIT config to the runner execution script via
command-line arguments using xargs. This included the JIT token in the
transient systemd unit file generated by systemd-run, which sometimes
failed with "Failed to resolve unit specifiers" errors. These issues are
hard to reproduce locally, but may be caused by template expansion
limits or token size.

We take direct control over the unit file instead of relying on
systemd-run’s transient unit generation, to better understand and debug
any related issues.

We now pass the JIT config via a file. This is more reliable for large
strings and avoids leaking sensitive tokens into the unit description.

This change is currently behind a feature flag. Once verified in
production, we’ll move the file creation to the image generation step.
ellipsis_summary:
----

> Switch JIT config passing to file-based method in `github_runner.rb`, controlled by a feature flag, with updated tests in `github_runner_spec.rb`.

title: Switch to multi phase login
description:
Multi phase login is the practice where you first ask for the login (email) and not the password, and after you know the related account, you show the options available for login to that account.

Multi phase login allows social login and OIDC login to be part of the normal login flow. Once we know the related account, we can show the authentication options for the account, and not include options that are not available. If the account does not have a password and is only connected to one social login provider, then the password field does not display, and the only button is the button login to the social login provider.

For accounts that only allow password authentication, multi phase login results in an extra step during login. However, I think it's better to support non-password authentication as part of the normal login flow.

A minor improvement I made during this process is if the user enters their login, but cannot remember their password, if they click the "Forgot your password?" link, their email address is already filled in.

Ideally, the login field would be have the readonly attribute during the second login phase.  However, I found that this negatively affects password managers such as 1password.  So I didn't mark the field as readonly.  I left the handling of the readonly attribute as boolean, in case we want to use readonly attributes elsewhere.

This required relatively few spec changes outside of the auth tests, since almost all tests that test for logged in accounts use the login helper method.

Here's what the UI looks like.  For the case where both password and another form of login are supported, I wonder whether it would be better to have the other forms of login under the "Sign in" button instead of above it.

Initial Login page:

![localhost_3000_login(iPhone XR)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6046ae5f-27d4-466d-ae41-e1965276ab37)

Only Password Authentication Supported:

![localhost_3000_login(iPhone XR) (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eda86aa0-44df-492f-9e60-94556cb9afcc)

Only OIDC Supported:

![localhost_3000_login(iPhone XR) (2)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f743f728-b20d-4c33-85df-3d1ceef65e8f)

Password and OIDC Supported: 

![localhost_3000_login(iPhone XR) (3)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e421a0f-5d3f-421e-a04b-d31b46ab15ef)
ellipsis_summary:
Implements multi-phase login to separate email and password input, supporting social and OIDC logins, with UI and test updates.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:
>     - Implements multi-phase login in `clover.rb`, asking for email first, then showing available login options.
>     - Updates `login.erb` to conditionally render password and social login options based on email input.
>     - If only one login method is available, it is automatically selected.
>     - Pre-fills email in "Forgot your password?" link.
>   - **UI**:
>     - `login.erb` updated to show login options after email is entered.
>     - Login field not set to readonly to support password managers.
>   - **Tests**:
>     - Updates in `auth_spec.rb` and `clover_web_spec.rb` to reflect multi-phase login.
>     - Adds tests for OIDC login flow in `auth_spec.rb`.
>

title: Ensure OIDC nonce does not repeat
description:
Currently, the nonce is randomly generated with 32 bytes, so statistically it should not run result in a duplicate nonce until 256**16 nonces have been generated. While that's probably fine, it's better to use an approach where nonces are not more likely to be duplicates over time.

This changes nonce generation to use a time-based component. The nonce is now nanosecond specific, and still has 13 bytes of randomness, which should be sufficiently random while still providing the quality that the chance of a duplicate nonce does not increase over time.
